title: Service Safety Standup Template and Decision Triggers (brief)
content:
One-pager + working kit for cross-team standups and hard decision triggers (working draft)

Context:
- We need a light-weight cadence that sits between feature teams and SRE to: maintain SLOs, triage risky rollouts, and run quick experiments to reduce P99 latency without regressing quality.
- This doc is intentionally tactical: templates, decision triggers, a short 6-week runbook and a prioritized experiment backlog.
- Purpose: reduce cognitive overhead for product/infra owners when incidents or SLO drift happen; standardize when to escalate to reliability war-room.

Objectives:
1) Create a predictable 15-min standup that surfaces signals and decisions for SLOs across 8 core services.
2) Define >=3 decision triggers that automatically flip a rollout or require a canary rollback.
3) Ship 3 micro-experiments in 6 weeks (batching config, cache TTL tweak, KV prefetch) to improve unit cost and P99.

Success criteria (how we’ll know this helped):
- Standup attendance >= 80% of listed stakeholders for 4 consecutive weeks.
- Number of escalation-worthy incidents reduced by 30% for services on pilot SLOs in 2 months.
- At least one experiment delivers >=10% P99 improvement without increasing 95th-percentile error.

Scope (what this covers):
- Core infra paths for text-generation and embedding endpoints; NOT model training or offline batch jobs.
- Applies to Hosted API + Dedicated pools in pilot regions (us-west1, eu-west1).

Stakeholders and quick RACI (one-liners):
- SRE lead: Priya Nair — owner (R) for cadence and war-room escalation
- Platform infra: Ethan Chen — C (consulted) on kernel and batching knobs
- Serving-runtime: Maya Patel — A (approver) for rolling changes to runtime config
- Product-hosted-api: Gabriel Ruiz — C (impacted team) for API-level routing policies
- Solutions Eng / SE: Caroline Simmons — I (informed) for customer impact messaging
- Oncall rotation: SRE oncall primary (R) for immediate mitigation steps

90-second standup template (15 min total):
- Quick signals (3 min): show 1-line SLO health (green/yellow/red) per service — 99% of the time this is automated dashboard snapshot.
- What changed in last 24h (3 min): deploys, config flips, unusual traffic patterns. Keep it bullety.
- Active mitigations & blockers (4 min): ongoing incidents, rollback plans, who’s executing.
- Decisions & next actions (4 min): any trigger hit? proceed/rollback/tune. Assign owners and ETA.
- Parking lot (1 min): items to move to async backlog or deep-dive slot.

Decision triggers (hard thresholds that require immediate attention):
1) SLO degradation: any service p99 latency slip >20% above baseline for 10 consecutive minutes -> escalate to war-room and pause new canaries.
2) Error spike: client-facing error-rate across a service >0.5% (absolute) for 5 minutes or >1% for 1 minute -> auto-notify and run circuit-breaker policy.
3) Budget/Cost: token-unit spend for batch generation >25% above forecast for rolling 1h window AND p95 latency not improved -> throttle non-critical workloads and notify owners.
Notes: thresholds are conservative for pilot; we will tune by service.

Triage/playbook snippets (quick):
- If trigger 1 (p99) -> verify KV cache effectiveness, check hot-shard counts, roll back last rollout if that changed inference kernel, run controlled canary on smaller shard.
- If trigger 2 (error) -> attach logs, identify top 3 failing endpoints, revert feature flag if tied to new call patterns.
- If trigger 3 (cost) -> enable short-term rate-limits for low-priority jobs, inspect batching config, possibly switch to cheaper model variant for non-critical paths.

6-week tactical plan (high-level iterations):
Week 0: kickoff + dashboard baseline capture + stakeholder alignment (create SLO dashboards for each service).
Week 1: define triggers per service + deploy standup cadence + dry run.
Week 2-3: run first two micro-experiments (batching tuning, prefix caching TTL). Collect metrics.
Week 4: implement rollout guard (automatic pause) wired into deployment pipeline; review results.
Week 5: run canary rollback template in staging and production drills.
Week 6: finalize playbooks, compile retro + next backlog.

Prioritized experiment backlog (short descriptions):
- EV1: Continuous-kv-prefix caching TTL sweep (owner: Maya) — target reduce p99 5-12% on chat flows.
- EV2: Batch window heuristics (owner: Ethan) — dynamic batch sizing based on seq length, aim to save tokens/cost.
- EV3: Fallback model routing policy (owner: Gabriel) — automatically route to quantized variant under load.
- EV4: Cost-aware throttling for non-critical endpoints (owner: Caroline) — manual->automated.

Monitoring/metrics to snapshot during standup (one-liners):
- SLO health: API success rate (error rate), p50/p95/p99 latencies, tail error breakdown.
- Cost signals: tokens/sec, cost-per-1k-tokens, queue depth.
- Capacity signals: GPU utilization per pool, hot-shard counts, batch size distribution.

Communication & escalation flow:
- Standup -> if red, open war-room (zoom link pinned in Slack #sre-service-safety) and ping exec-oncall.
- Customer impact template: short three-line blurb (what, who, mitigation ETA) + link to status page.
- Post-incident: short retro doc under Confluence + action owner list (due within 3 business days).

Operational checklist (quick):
- Dashboards configured and visible to all stakeholders.
- Standup calendar invite with link to runbook and last 24h snapshot.
- CI/CD guard in place to pause canaries (button + auto-pause hooks).
- Oncall rotation documented and backup contact.

Open questions / TODOs (working):
- Who owns tuning per-service thresholds long-term? (Ops or feature teams?) -> TODO: define in next stakeholder sync.
- Need a lightweight visualization for batch size vs latency distribution (Ethan to prototype).
- Confirm fallback model inventory for each endpoint (Gabriel to list).

Appendix: quick templates
- Standup invite description (copy/paste): "15-min SRE-Service Safety standup. Bring SLO snapshots, recent deploys, and any blockers. If red, escalate to war-room."
- War-room starter checklist (copy): link logs, assign recorder, set incident severity, set comm updates cadence (every 15 min).

Quick notes to self:
- Keep this doc short — move long-form playbooks to Confluence.
- Expect friction on thresholds; plan a 3-week tuning window.
- Run two simulated incidents during week 4 to validate escalations.

Linked tickets (starting seeds):
- SRE-4821: configure SLO dashboards for embedding-service
- SRE-4850: add auto-canary pause hook to deployment pipeline
- EXP-712: batch window experiment prototype

End.
